- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.27) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.10) or neutral — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lagged corrections: if true price drops after a forecast spike, reduce next forecast by 1–2% of the spike magnitude.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model forecasts a sharp rise after a spike, reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating volatility — reduce forecast by 1–3% for each day beyond 15 days.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment >0.36, model tends to overreact — apply a 2–5% downward correction to forecast if sentiment is high and price is rising.
